scientific_question: Does temporal complementarity among hydrological microhabitats buffer broad-scale residency by permitting within-area habitat-state tracking?
priority_design: individual-resolved movement with repeated hydrological surfaces within and beyond familiar home ranges

eligibility.taxa: wetland birds; rails preferred for primary biological continuity but taxonomic replication encouraged
required: repeated water-depth or equivalent hydrological state through time
enough spatial resolution to distinguish within-home-range shifts from broad relocation
baseline familiar area/home range definable without future movement outcomes
at least one period of meaningful hydrological change
preferred: multiple species or populations with different hydrological niche breadth
reject_if: only site-level detection histories are available for the primary test
hydrological state is measured only once
home range is defined using the same future relocation event used as response
temporal complementarity cannot be distinguished from mean habitat quality

primary_estimand: effect of lower-tail retained suitable area (HPI) on broad relocation after controlling mean habitat quality
mechanism_estimand: increase in within-home-range microhabitat switching during hydrological change

interpretation.mean_quality_only: generic habitat quality explanation; portfolio hypothesis not supported
interpretation.heterogeneity_increases_relocation: opposite ecological response; reject buffering prediction

no_rescue: do not redefine suitable-depth window or familiar area after inspecting relocation outcomes
